chapter: Original Dixieland Jazz Band: Chicago and New York
title: Personnel changes at Reisenweber's and in London: Robinson, Signorelli, Christian
summary: Piano changes after Ragas died, Edwards's army absence, Emil Christian's London records, and the Folies Bergere booking.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: and after you got to New York you had the same band as we stated now yeah the Rising Webbers were there any changes there ever in Rising Webbers?

no that was uh except when Regis passed away Russell Robinson joined the band and uh he left and they got Frankie Signorelli I was in the army at that time and they got Frankie Signorelli to take his place then when they went to Europe Russell wished to go to Europe and he did go for I think six months and he came back and they got a man by the name of the Jones Billy Jones to play piano in London and then when they came back I booked them at the uh Foley-Bergé that was 50th in Broadway for the Salvin brothers Salvin father and son and uh Russell came along with us that's where he composed Margie and singing the blues and a number of other songs
I was wondering when you were out of the band in the army who took your place? Emil Christian played trombone only Christian that's right and uh did Christian make any
records in this country do you know? no no he did make some in uh London I don't believe they turned out any too well through no fault of his through no fault of Emil's

I have heard them and it seems to me he plays very close to your parts on them yes you must have listened very carefully to your records were there any other changes after Robinson came in? Signorelli came with us
